Usage: rig scope slice create [options] <mission> <slug>

Create a new slice with SPEC.md, slice.yaml, PROGRESS.md, PROOF.md, and proof/.
Conventions SSOT: docs/reference/sdlc-conventions.md (installed:
$OPENRIG_HOME/reference/sdlc-conventions.md).

Arguments:
  mission                             Mission name
  slug                                Short slug (becomes the folder name's
                                      suffix)

Options:
  --template <kind>                   Template: placeholder | bug-fix |
                                      backlog-deprecation | backlog-tech-debt |
                                      release-feature | research (default:
                                      "placeholder")
  --title <text>                      Display title (defaults to titlecased
                                      slug)
  --intent <text>                     Authored intent stored in SPEC.md
                                      frontmatter (defaults to title)
  --depends-on <dot-id...>            Advisory build-order dependencies on
                                      sibling slice dot-IDs
  --execution-depends-on <dot-id...>  Build-order edges on sibling slice dot-IDs
                                      written to slice.yaml
                                      execution.depends_on, which proof
                                      readiness reads (not copied to SPEC.md)
  --readme-only                       Write progress_rail: readme-only in README
                                      frontmatter instead of scaffolding
                                      PROGRESS.md
  --json                              Machine-readable output
  -h, --help                          display help for command

Workspace: the parent option --workspace selects the missions root this command reads.
  rig scope --workspace <project root> slice create ...
A project root uses its project.yaml missions.root, else its missions/ folder; a
folder named missions is used as is. Use it for a catalog project, for example
$(rig config get workspace.projects_root)/<project>. Without --workspace,
OPENRIG_WORK_ROOT applies, then the configured workspace.slices_root.
